title: Overlap Finder
one_liner: Paste your subscription list and see which tools an AI-assistant workspace could replace and the potential monthly savings.
speaker: Peter Diamandis
context: Anthropic launched AI-built spreadsheets, whiteboards, data dashboards and meeting tools, plus connectors to popular work apps. The hosts said software is being absorbed by AI assistants and Microsoft shares fell.
demo: The user pastes or types their tools with seats and monthly price. The page sorts each tool into a category (dashboards, whiteboard, forms, notes, slides and so on) and labels it 'likely replaceable', 'partially' or 'keep', with reasons. It totals the potential savings and produces a migration checklist they can print.
data_plan: The customer's own subscription list and prices. The category-to-feature mapping is a bundled, editable rule table written by the builder. No episode numbers are used in the calculation.
risks: AI features may be immature or beta, so replacements could break workflows. Vendor lock-in simply moves to the AI vendor. Savings per client may be small.

figures.meaning: drop in Microsoft shares on the day of the Anthropic launch
figures.said: Microsoft shares fell 3.5% on the news.

figures.meaning: Office revenue versus Microsoft's total annual revenue, as stated by a host
figures.said: office is 90 billion dollars a year revenue

acceptance: Entering 5 tools with seats and prices produces a table labelling each one replaceable, partial or keep, with a reason
The total potential monthly and annual savings update immediately when a tool's verdict is toggled
An example button fills in a sample 12-tool stack, clearly marked as an example
Clicking 'Print checklist' shows a migration checklist listing only the tools marked replaceable
On a 375px-wide screen the table stacks into cards without horizontal scrolling

opportunity.title: Seat Shed
opportunity.one_liner: Audits a small company's software subscriptions and replaces the ones an AI assistant's built-in sheets, boards and connectors now cover.
opportunity.customer: Operations managers at US companies with 15–150 staff that pay for 15 or more SaaS tools
opportunity.problem: Companies keep paying per-seat for dashboards, whiteboards, form builders and reporting add-ons that the AI plan they already pay for can now do. Nobody has time to map out what overlaps and run a safe migration.
opportunity.revenue_model: Fixed-fee audit of about $1,500 (estimate), plus an optional 20% share of the first year's savings for migration work (estimate).
opportunity.why_now: The episode reports AI vendors shipping sheets, whiteboards, dashboards and app connectors directly, and says markets reacted to the threat to traditional office and SaaS revenue.
